title: Serpent, go away

words.meaning: at the end of the sacrifice

samasa.meaning: at the end of the sacrifice

translation.literal: Serpent, creep away; good luck to you; go, serpent of great venom, remembering Āstīka’s word at the end of Janamejaya’s sacrifice.
translation.readable: Go away, serpent, and good luck to you; go, venomous one — remember what Āstīka asked at the end of Janamejaya’s sacrifice.

sandhi_exceptions.note: at the break between the two halves of the verse, where the recitation pauses; the witness leaves the vowels unjoined

meaning: The third verse against serpents speaks to the snake itself, politely: it wishes it well and sends it away, reminding it of the word given to Āstīka when he ended King Janamejaya’s serpent sacrifice. The verse assumes the story behind jaratkāroḥ: the serpents, saved by Āstīka, promised to spare those who remember him.
in_the_rite: Step sarpa-rakṣā, all three services, the last of the three verses.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Anuṣṭubh (śloka). S’s third pāda, जनमेजयस्य यज्ञान्ते, has nine syllables; M’s जनमेजय-यज्ञान्ते has the regular eight.

notes.label: direct
notes.text: M reads the first line differently: अपसर्प सर्प भद्रं ते दूरं गच्छ महायशाः (‘go far away, O famous one’); the variants are listed in corrections.json.
